name: Question 4
problem:
Suppose we would like to find an integrating factor to convert the differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=4xy+3x
$$

into an exact equation using an integrating factor. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.For a differential equation of the form

$$
P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y=0,
$$

we have that if

$$
{{field-1}}=g(x)
$$

where $g(x)$ is independent of $y,$ then an integrating factor for the equation is

$$
I(x)={{field-2}}
$$

where $\operatorname{exp}⁡(x)$ denotes the exponential function ${e}^{x}.$

Question 4

Suppose we would like to find an integrating factor to convert the differential equation y′=4xy+3x into an exact equation using an integrating factor. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.For a differential equation of the form P(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy=0, we have that if

1Q(∂P∂y+∂Q∂x)
1Q(∂P∂y−∂Q∂x)
1Q(∂P∂y+∂Q∂x)
1P(∂P∂y−∂Q∂x)
1P(∂P∂y+∂Q∂x)
{(1Q(∂P∂y−∂Q∂x))(S0)}=g(x)

where g(x) is independent of y, then an integrating factor for the equation is
exp⁡(∫g(x)dx)
exp⁡(g(x))
exp⁡(−∫g(x)dx)
exp⁡(−g(x))
exp⁡(∫g(x)dx)
I(x)={(exp⁡(−∫g(x)dx))(S1)} where exp⁡(x) denotes the exponential function ex.
